chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'How do you see it for me to perform the Talbiyah?' He said to me, 'If you wish, you specify [separately], and if you wish, you do not specify anything.' I said to him, 'What do you do yourself?' He said, 'I combine them, so I say: 'Here I am, O God, with Hajj and Umrah together.' Then he said, 'Indeed, I have told your companions something other than this.'

key_terms.أَجْمَعُهُمَا: I combine them (referring to the two pilgrimages)
key_terms.أُهِلَّ: To perform the Talbiyah (verbal declaration of intent for pilgrimage)
key_terms.سَمَّيْتَ: You specify (naming the specific pilgrimage separately)
key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ: Here I am (the opening phrase of the Talbiyah)

ai.seo_question: How should one perform the Talbiyah when combining Hajj and Umrah?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi highlights the flexibility in the ritual declaration (Talbiyah) for Qiran, where the Imam demonstrates his personal preference for combining Hajj and Umrah in one utterance while acknowledging the permissibility of specifying them separately. The concluding remark, 'I have not said this to your companions,' alludes to the scholarly principle of Taqiyya (dissimulation) or contextual variation, indicating that his public ruling to others may have differed due to political or social circumstances. This underscores the dynamic nature of Ja'fari jurisprudence, where the Imam's practice serves as a primary source of law alongside his reported statements.
